Priya: Quick update — ran the ablation matrix for kernel selection + batching on our long-context prefill workload. Short summary below, full logs linked.
Kai: awesome, was this replay or synthetic? any variance from the last run?
Priya: Replay harness (stable seed) + a synthetic run with the same seq-length histogram. Replay shows a 12% p99 regression when kernelB is picked for prefill-heavy requests.
Jon: hmm 12% p99 is pretty material. Is that across single-GPU serving or multi-GPU? batch sizes?
Priya: Single GPU (A100-40), steady-state batching. Batch-size distribution: mostly 1-4 during prefill because of long sequences, a tail of 8 for short queries. We saw kernel flip at seq_len >= 1024 — runtime prefers kernelB for the attention path.
Marta: Can you paste the commands used for the harness? I want to replay locally.
Priya: sure:
```
./replay_harness --trace replay/longmix_2026.trace --model redwood-13b --seed 42 \
  --kernel-policy ablate --kernels kernelA,kernelB --out out/1950123456
```
Priya: Also ran synthetic with this generator to match seq histogram:
```
python tools/gen_synth.py --hist histograms/longmix.json --qps 80 --duration 900
```
Kai: Do we have flamegraphs / NVTX stamps? would help identify where the regression sits (prefill KV write vs attention compute).
Priya: Yup. perf-bot uploaded a quick profile: /bench/results/1950123456/flame.svg — main delta is in "attention_dispatch" and "kv_cache_write" edged up when kernelB used.
perf-bot: Profiling summary: median token latency +7%, p99 +12% when kernelB used on prefill-dominant traces. Hot functions: attention_dispatch, kv_cache_write, cuda_memcpy_async.
Jon: Interesting that kv_write increased. Could be different memory access pattern in kernelB that hurts KV streaming for long sequences.
Marta: Did you try forcing kernelA for prefill segments only (seq_len >= 512) to see if we can get the best of both worlds?
Priya: Yes — config flag forced kernelA for prefill; that recovered p99 to within 1% of baseline but slightly worsened median by ~2% due to more kernel switches.
Kai: Kernel switch overhead vs per-token efficiency tradeoff. We need apples-to-apples: same model binary, same memory allocator and cupy/cupti settings.
Jon: Agreed. Also synthetic vs replay discrepancy suggests replay includes cache-warm effects and real batching shapes. Are we sure replay harness preserves inter-arrival time jitter?
Priya: We replayed original timestamps, preserving client pacing. Synthetic was Poisson with same mean QPS — that removed burstiness and reduced kernel switch rate.
Marta: Action items:
- Run apples-to-apples compile: build kernels with identical allocator flags and priming memory pools. (Jon)
- Add instrumentation counters: kernel switch count, KV write bytes per op, per-kernel memcpys. (Kai)
- Run targeted experiment forcing kernelA for prefill >= 512, measure switch overhead at varying qps. (Priya)
- Compare replay vs synthetic under matched burstiness (use original timing) and produce a short note. (Marta)
Priya: Also flagged a perf regression ticket (ENG-PRF-621) with baseline attachments. Adding links in the ticket.
Kai: For the apples-to-apples compile, we should pin cuBLAS/cuDNN and the compiler flags — different JIT heuristics can change loop unrolling and memory layout.
Jon: For profiling, NVTX + CUPTI traces are best. nvprof is deprecated so don't use that. Use nsight-sys to capture timeline and perf counters.
Marta: If KV write is the issue, we should prototype async batching of KV writes: coalesce writes for concurrent prefill windows. Might reduce memcpy overhead.
Priya: Good idea — I'll add a quick patch to coalesce writes in the runtime and run smoke. If it reduces memcpy time we can upstream to the kernel selection policy.
perf-bot: Reminder: leave run metadata in bench/meta/1950123456.json (model, commit, kernel hashes, hardware).
Kai: Thanks, Priya. Can you drop the main p99 numbers + config into the ticket and ping me? I'll take the apples-to-apples compile.
Priya: Will do. TL;DR: kernelB looks better for short-high-throughput, but for prefill-dominant long-context traffic kernelA gives better tail. Need more apples-to-apples tests and KV write instrumentation before we change routing defaults. :thinking:
Marta: Great notes — moving this to a short tech RFC after we finish the ablation runs. :memo:
